The observed peak at 790 nm with a sharp drop at shorter wavelengths is characteristic of the Lyman-alpha emission line (rest wavelength 121.6 nm) and the associated Lyman-alpha forest. The redshift is calculated as:
\[
1+z = \frac{\lambda_{\text{obs}}}{\lambda_{\text{rest}}} = \frac{790}{121.6} \approx 6.5 \quad \Rightarrow \quad z \approx 5.5.
\]
In a flat ΛCDM universe with \(H_0 = 70\ \text{km s}^{-1}\text{Mpc}^{-1}\), \(\Omega_m = 0.3\), and \(\Omega_\Lambda = 0.7\), the comoving distance is:
\[
D_c = \frac{c}{H_0} \int_0^z \frac{dz'}{\sqrt{\Omega_m(1+z')^3 + \Omega_\Lambda}}.
\]
With \(c/H_0 \approx 4.286\ \text{Gpc}\), numerical integration of the dimensionless distance integral up to \(z = 5.5\) yields approximately 1.88, giving \(D_c \approx 8.07\ \text{Gpc}\). This rounds to 8 Gpc.

Answer: B
